abstract:
As chatbots driven by large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in everyday contexts, their ability to recover from errors through effective apologies is critical to maintaining user trust and satisfaction. In a preregistered study with Prolific workers (
                    N
                    = 162), we examine user preferences for three types of apologies (
                    rote
                    ,
                    explanatory
                    , and
                    empathic
                    ) issued in response to three categories of common LLM mistakes (
                    bias
                    ,
                    unfounded fabrication
                    , and
                    factual errors
                    ). We designed a pairwise experiment in which participants evaluated chatbot responses consisting of an initial error, a subsequent apology, and a resolution. Explanatory apologies were generally preferred, but this varied by context and user. In the bias scenario, empathic apologies were favored for acknowledging emotional impact, while hallucinations, though seen as serious, elicited no clear preference, reflecting user uncertainty. Our findings show the complexity of effective apology in AI systems. We discuss key insights such as personalization and calibration that future systems must navigate to meaningfully repair trust.

ur.ai_reason: LLM道歉用户偏好，预注册实验(N=162)
ur.tldr: 预注册实验(N=162)比较用户对LLM聊天机器人三种道歉方式(机械式、解释式、共情式)在偏见、虚构、事实错误三类失误下的偏好。解释式道歉总体更受青睐,但偏见场景中用户倾向共情式以承认情绪影响,幻觉场景则无明确偏好,反映AI道歉需个性化与校准以有效修复信任。

title: Who’s Sorry Now: User Preferences Among Rote, Empathic, and Explanatory Apologies from LLM Chatbots
title_zh: "现在谁在道歉"：用户对大语言模型聊天机器人机械式、共情式与解释性道歉的偏好
